about: Hearth's building sheet style sheet as data (HISTORY.md #805 to #807). validate.mjs reads all of it; buildings.py reads tiers, snow and the sheet. A frame is drawn at one frame pixel to one map pixel, so its sides and its anchor are whole tiles (T, read from js/core.js). Every opaque pixel is a js/render.js colour times one of the tiers (the side a face is turned to: #805), within tolerance levels (`lifted` holds the ones the wiring took out of render.js with the drawings that used them, read off js/render.js at 4786389; spec.mjs adds them to the palette), and every pixel is fully opaque or fully clear. `was` is the box, in map pixels from the building's tile corner, that render.js's procedural drawing covered, as [x0, y0, x1, y1] (the mill without its sails, which stay drawn); a frame's drawn box keeps its width and height within `scaleTolerance` of it and its foot on the same row (the common plan's scale rule, and draw() sorts by the foot). A snow frame is snow and nothing else, and only where its building is drawn. maxKiB is KiB x 1024, maxSide the longest side in pixels.
